questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The incident was narrated by somebody to Naresh.

options.text: Somebody was narrating the incident to Naresh.
Somebody narrated the incident to Naresh.
Somebody was about to narrate the incident to Naresh.
Somebody will narrate the incident to Naresh.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Somebody narrated the incident to Naresh**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are a few things to keep in mind when changing a sentence from **passive to active voice**.

 
 
• The **agent **in the passive voice becomes the subject(doer of the action) of the active voice.
 
• In the given sentence, "**somebody**" becomes the **subject **in the active voice.
 
• We can omit the usage of "**by**" in the active voice. We use the preposition "by" to show the **agent **in the passive voice.
 
• We can also omit the usage of "to be" forms in the active voice. So we can omit "**was**" which is the past tense of "to be" in the given sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the **simple past tense.**
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is** option 2.**

​The correct sentence is: *Somebody narrated the incident to Naresh.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__***

__
 
• वाक्य को passive to active voice में बदलते समय कुछ बातों का ध्यान रखना चाहिए।

 
 
• **passive voice** में एजेंट **active voice** का विषय (कार्रवाई का कर्ता) बन जाता है।
 
• दिए गए वाक्य में, "somebody" सक्रिय आवाज में विषय बन जाता है।
 
• हम **active voice** में "by" के उपयोग को छोड़ सकते हैं। एजेंट को **passive voice** में दिखाने के लिए हम "by" **preposition **का उपयोग करते हैं।
 
• हम active voice में **"****to be**" फॉर्म के उपयोग को भी छोड़ सकते हैं।
 
• इसलिए हम "was" को छोड़ सकते हैं जो दिए गए वाक्य में "**to be**" का भूत काल है।
 
 
 
• दिया गया वाक्य simple past tense का है।

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

I was waiting __from__ two hours.
questions.solution:

__
 
• In the given sentence, the usage of the **preposition **"**from**" is incorrect.
 
• We use the **preposition** '**from' **to show where **something starts or originates**. We also use **from** to show movement from one thing to another.
 
• In the given sentence, we need to use the preposition "**for**".
 
• We use the preposition 'for' to state how long something lasts or continues.
 
 
• **Example**: *I waited at the metro station **for **__about 45 minutes so that I could catch the first metro.*
 
 
 
• We also use the preposition "**for**" as a conjunction to link the** first and second clauses of a sentence**.
 
• The implied meaning of the given sentence is that the speaker is expressing how long they waited.

**The correct sentence is**: *I was waiting **__for__**** **two hours.*

Hence, the correct answer is **option 3.**

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

B. There is no telling when a squabble between a couple may aggravate and escalate into something ugly, which when witnessed by a child, might devastate them gravely.

C. There's no relationship that does not falter.

D. Arguments, disagreements and conflicts are extremely common even in a healthy relationship.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**CDAB**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the **correct sequence **of the passage.

 
 
• **Statement C **is the opening sentence of the passage as it begins with a **general opinion** about relationships. Opening statements are usually general statements about a topic. The given sentence is a general statement about relationships.
 
• **Statement D **is the second sentence of the passage it **elaborates on the general statement** in the previous sentence. The authors state that arguments, disagreements and conflicts are extremely common even in a healthy relationship.
 
• **Statement A ** is the third sentence of the passage as it begins with a **conjunction **"but" depicting a contrast to the previous statement. The given sentence talks about** the negative impact **of arguments, disagreements, and conflicts of the parents on their children.
 
• **Statement B **is the concluding statement of the passage as it **summarizes the core ideas** in one sentence. The author states that there is no telling when a squabble between a couple may aggravate and escalate into something ugly, which when witnessed by a child, might devastate them gravely.
 
 

​Hence, the correct answer is **option 4.**
